## Moist physics coupling evidence {#sec-ch15-ch10-tests}

Moist verification needs separate checks for phase adjustment, species repair and transport.
A local repair can conserve mass without validating the coupled kinetics discussed in @sec-ch10.

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Connect the chapter's claims to executable assertions.

**Data.** Test inputs and thresholds; no new solver measurements.

**Placement.** Verification outside the simulation step.

**Activation.** Select the named tests; this catalogue changes no defaults.

**Guarantee / limits.** Source coverage does not establish a runtime pass.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer distinguishes report checks from solver tests.
:::

### Derivation

The numerical derivations remain in the linked chapter. The error and conservation identities for interpreting
these tests are written out in the opening section of @sec-ch15; this inventory introduces no additional update equation.

### Numerical method

Read the assertion and its registration, then run the selected test in a build of the code pin.
Record device, precision, process count and skipped cases separately. @fig-ch15-evidence shows why an independent
formula check cannot establish that the compiled implementation ran.

: Assertion definitions for this catalogue. {#tbl-ch15-ch10-tests-sources}

The numbered source entries above map directly to the Tests table. CTest registration names and environments
come from `setup_test`, `snapy_add_python_test` and the explicit entries in
{{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}. The `.release` suffix denotes a Release build;
other configurations use their build suffix through `setup_test`
({{< code cmake/macros/macro_setup_test.cmake >}}).

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_wall_saturation.release` | Wall phase change preserves total energy and water | relative drift below $10^{-12}$ | Source assertion 1 |
| `test_condensate_conservation.release` | Two parents pay the stoichiometric debit; cloud deficit is cleared | mass allclose $10^{-12}$; parents $10^{-6}$; cloud exact | Source assertion 2 |
| `test_eos.release` | Net-deficit column is rejected without changing the state | failure code 1; unchanged vector | Source assertion 3 |
| `test_scalar.release` | Transported scalar ratio stays bounded on both sides | float32 $10^{-5}$; float64 $10^{-12}$ | Source assertion 4 |
| `test_sedimentation_guards.release` | Rising cloud is taken from below | absolute error at most $10^{-9}$ times reference | Source assertion 5 |
| `test_check_redo_parallel.release` | A retry decision and rollback are shared by ranks | exact tensor equality | Source assertion 6 |

: Acceptance criteria read from the code pin; no solver pass is claimed. {#tbl-ch15-ch10-tests-assertions}

The parent-debit tolerances above distinguish conserved total mass from the individual parent values; they
are not float64/float32 alternatives. The test uses both tolerances in each device/dtype case.
The existing `src/snapy_report/ch10/{fixvapor,borrow,kinetics,tracer,sed,redo}_check.py` scripts
check ported formulas. Their fixture comparison is separate from a tolerance test of physical quantities.

### Limits

These selected assertions do not establish a full kinetics-step mass/energy budget, an evaporation-rate
validation, saturation across a decomposed wall or MPS sedimentation. The broader repair registrations
remain in the test index (@sec-appc); runtime combinations remain in @sec-ch12-matrix.
